summary.intent: Clean up stale information after merging release PRs (#401, #379/#402) and decide what hardening work comes next, then fix the duplicate release run that failed with E167 after #402 merged during the 0.16.0 release.
summary.outcome: Confirmed 0.16.0 is intact (GitHub release, crates.io, four tags), diagnosed the duplicate run as a per-SHA workflow concurrency gap, and committed a signed fix changing the group to a single fixed `release` name with docs/releasing.md updated. The stale NEXT-WORK.md could not be written from the worktree and the PR was not yet opened or proven live.

repo: The workflow-level concurrency group in callisto-release.yml was `release-${{ github.sha }}`, so it only deduped reruns of the same push and never serialized different pushes.
The `execute` job has its own `release-execute` group that serializes executes, but it is too late because `release pending` already selected the release before the lock.
The per-SHA group existed because a shared group drops queued release merges (GitHub keeps one pending run per group). That is now harmless since every run asks `release pending` what is unfinished.
E167 fires when a second run rebuilds artifacts that differ from assets the first run already uploaded.
E180: GitHub Actions' token cannot push tags at a commit that is not a branch tip, so automated drain cannot recover non-tip releases and a person must push tags.
The release PR created by the workflow token gets no CI checks, so CI must be re-triggered before merging a release PR.
A guard blocks writing to the shared checkout (.claude/plans) from a worktree.
Workflow-contract test output contains passing tests with 'failed' in their names, so the real exit status must be checked.

code.finding: Workflow-level concurrency changed from per-SHA group to a fixed `release` group with cancel-in-progress false so pushes during a release queue behind it.
Guide's description of reruns/concurrency updated to match the new single release group.

workflow: Read the plan file and in-repo roadmap before recommending next work rather than relying on memory, and flag that items were not re-verified.
When test output is noisy, confirm the real exit status separately instead of trusting text matches.
Work done from a worktree can be blocked from writing to the shared checkout; stage the file in a tmp dir and give the user a copy command.

friction: Could not write the rewritten NEXT-WORK.md directly because the guard blocks writes to the shared checkout from the worktree.
The concurrency fix cannot be tested locally; it needs two real pushes in quick succession.
Test output with 'failed' in test names made the contract run look like a failure.
Earlier `.claude/settings.json` edit (entire doctor hook-timeout) had to be reverted and was left in the job tmp directory.
open_items: Open the PR for the concurrency fix and note in it that the first proof is live.
User must copy the rewritten NEXT-WORK.md into .claude/plans/ and the memory index entry stays marked stale until then.
Edge case: a manual dispatch with an explicit `release_source_sha` could be replaced in the queue by a push-triggered run; redispatch if so.
Remove the dead `pending_pr_label` action input and its test, with a changeset since it is a public input.
Delete stale local branches and worktrees (several squash-merged, needing -D).

Hardening backlog: dispatch CI on the release PR branch, decide on a recovery credential for non-tip releases, re-audit spec drift and #290 guard gaps, T12 real-path registry tests, native fixture evidence.

Feature gaps: private workspace-root package.json listed as a package, shared tag/release title for fixed groups (E194), onboarding timing, private/HTML-only PyPI indexes, npm channel promotion/checksums/wrapper bump severity decisions.
Small cleanups: split registry_argv.rs per package manager, replace matrix.rs 18-triple table with rustc target facts, accept ADR 12.
Org variable TAP_APP_CLIENT_ID and secret TAP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY still exist on GitHub; remove Callisto's access if desired.
